This is characteristic of free radical addition mechanisms (especially with NBS), which proceed via a radical intermediate that favors the less substituted carbon due to stability of radicals.

This is known as anti-Markovnikov addition — but note, the question asks specifically about the orientation of the bromine atom.

The bromine ends up on the less substituted carbon — which is exactly the non-Markovnikov orientation.
